content.text:
Silhouette: Four-legged gray wolf frame. Host frame: the gray wolf sets the outline, body size and overall frame. A single creature that combines a crab and a gray wolf. Head of the gray wolf, fully visible and uncluttered, with clear, discernible eyes. Details: gray wolf body and legs, with its own dense fur on the face, neck, shoulders, belly, hips, legs and tail, plain coat, no stripes or spots; from the crab, as parts and materials on the gray wolf's own body: claws grown from the front feet, each front foot ends in a pincer held folded against the foot when the animal walks — heavy, knobbed, hard-shelled claws with a fixed and a moving finger, large evenly sized claws with black tips; hard, glossy chitin plates with fine seams in its own colors, grown from the skin as the gray wolf's own covering over the back and flanks. It replaces the gray wolf's dense fur there and conforms to the gray wolf's body: one broad, fused carapace shield over the gray wolf's shoulders and back, its edge like the donor's pie-crust frilled edge with rounded lobes, with short jointed plates on each limb section, sized to the gray wolf's body, joined by flexible cuticle at every joint. Every covered part keeps the gray wolf's own length and shape; the dense fur stops at the covering's edge, and the face, neck, shoulders, belly, hips, legs and tail keep the gray wolf's own dense fur. The covering follows the body's own shape and bends at every joint. Declared fiction: arthropod parts at large size, shown with thick supporting legs. Bilaterally symmetrical, recognizable limbs, visible sense organs. Habitat cue (rocky coast): dark back and light belly (strong countershading). Prosaic detail: natural lighting, feet in firm contact with the ground with a soft shadow, normal wear on hooves, claws and skin. One creature, full body, side three-quarter view, plain light background, natural history illustration.
Aspect ratio: 1:1.

summary.text:
**Designing crab-wolf hybrid**
I'm shaping the creature around a gray wolf silhouette, keeping the four-legged frame and full wolf head with clear eyes, then adding heavy crab pincers at the front feet and dense, plain fur across the body.
**Designing armored wolf hybrid**
I'm shaping a gray wolf with a broad chitin carapace over the back and flanks, pie-crust frilled edges, and jointed plates on the limbs, while keeping fur on the head, neck, belly, legs, and tail, and giving the front feet folded pincer claws with black tips for a natural history illustration.
**Refining hybrid limb details**
I'm planning a regeneration to adjust the hybrid so only the front limbs have pincers and jointed plates, while the hind legs keep normal fur for a more accurate look.
